name: Client-only code on a dedicated server
aliases: invalid dist, client-only mod on server, client class on server, RuntimeDistCleaner
cause: A mod that only works in the game client is on the server, or a server mod wrongly loads client-only game code.
fix: Remove client-only mods (for example Rubidium, Oculus, Mod Menu) from the server's mods folder; if the named mod is meant for servers, update it or report it to its author.

name: Missing or wrong-version mod dependency (Forge)
aliases: missing dependency, missing library mod, Actual version: [MISSING], mandatory dependencies, needs newer Forge
cause: A mod needs another mod, or a newer Forge, that isn't installed or is the wrong version.
fix: Install the mod named after "Mod ID" in a version inside "Expected range"; if the Mod ID is forge, update Forge itself.

name: Fabric mod is missing a required mod
aliases: missing dependency, requires fabric-api, Incompatible mods found
cause: A Fabric mod needs another mod, such as Fabric API, that isn't installed.
fix: Install the mod named in the line, in the version it asks for. Lines that only say "recommends" are suggestions, not the crash.

name: Fabric mod built for a different version
aliases: wrong version, version mismatch, requires version, Incompatible mods found
signature: but only the wrong version is present:
cause: A mod was built for a different version of Minecraft, or of another mod, than the server has.
fix: Download the build of the mod that matches the server's version, or change the server's version.

name: Mixin failed to apply
aliases: mixin error, MixinTransformerError, Critical injection failure, InjectionError, mixin apply failed
signature: MixinTransformerError: An unexpected critical error was encountered
cause: A mod couldn't patch the game's code, usually because it was built for another version or clashes with another mod.
fix: Read the Caused by lines below it for the mod named in the "mixins.json" part; update that mod, or remove the mod it clashes with.

name: Server ran out of memory
aliases: OOM, out of memory, Java heap space, OutOfMemoryError, not enough RAM
cause: The server used up all the memory (RAM) Java was allowed to give it.
fix: Give the server more RAM by raising -Xmx in its start command (modded servers usually need several GB).

name: 32-bit Java limits the server's RAM
aliases: 32-bit Java, Client VM, can't allocate more RAM, 247 MB heap
cause: The server runs on 32-bit Java, which can't use more than about 1.5 GB of RAM, so modded servers run out of memory.
fix: Uninstall 32-bit Java, install 64-bit Java, then set -Xmx to the RAM you want.

name: Watchdog: one server tick took too long
aliases: server hang, watchdog crash, Watching Server, max-tick-time, tick took 60.00 seconds
signature: ServerHangWatchdog detected that a single server tick took
cause: One server tick ran for 60 seconds or more (or start-up ran past the limit), so the watchdog shut the server down on purpose. Common causes: heavy world generation or /locate, huge saves, lag machines, too many entities, a slow host.
fix: Check what the "Server thread" was doing in the report and fix that; set max-tick-time=-1 in server.properties only while testing.

name: Server needs Java 21
aliases: UnsupportedClassVersionError, class file version 65.0, wrong Java version
signature: (class file version 65.0), this version of the Java Runtime only recognizes class file versions up to 61.0
cause: The server needs Java 21 but is running on Java 17.
fix: Install Java 21 and start the server with it.

name: Server needs Java 25
aliases: UnsupportedClassVersionError, class file version 69.0, wrong Java version, Java 25
signature: (class file version 69.0), this version of the Java Runtime only recognizes class file versions up to 65.0
cause: Minecraft 26.1 and newer need Java 25, but the server is running on Java 21.
fix: Install Java 25 and start the server with it; on hosting panels, check that the Java 25 setting really applied.

name: Ticking entity crash
aliases: ticking entity, entity crash, Entity being ticked, corrupted entity
cause: An entity (a mob, item or player) crashed while the server was updating it, usually because of broken data or a mod bug.
fix: Back up the world, then remove the entity named under "Entity being ticked" using its type and coordinates (or set removeErroringEntities=true in forge-server.toml); if a mod appears in the error, update or remove it.

name: Ticking block entity crash
aliases: ticking block entity, ticking tile entity, Block entity being ticked, machine crash
cause: A block that stores data, such as a machine, pipe or chest, crashed while the server was updating it, usually because of a mod bug.
fix: Back up the world, then update the mod that owns the block or remove the block; on Forge, the remove-erroring setting in forge-server.toml can delete it.

name: Exception ticking world
aliases: ticking world, world tick crash
cause: Something crashed while the server was updating the world; the mod named in the stack trace is usually the culprit.
fix: Find the first mod package in the stack trace and update or remove that mod; restore a backup if the world data is broken.

name: Fabric mod failed while starting (entrypoint error)
aliases: entrypoint error, Could not execute entrypoint stage, mod init crash
signature: Could not execute entrypoint stage 'main' due to errors, provided by
cause: A Fabric mod threw an error while starting up. The mod named after "provided by" is where it happened, and the last Caused by line says why.
fix: Read the last Caused by line, then update that mod and its library mods to versions made for each other, or remove it.

name: Mod built for a different Minecraft version
aliases: NoSuchMethodError, NoSuchFieldError, wrong mod version, mod for older Minecraft
cause: A mod built for another Minecraft version tries to use game code that doesn't exist in this version.
fix: Install the build of the mod made for the server's exact Minecraft version.

name: Hybrid server (Arclight, Mohist) breaks mods
aliases: Arclight, Mohist, hybrid server, plugins and mods together
cause: Hybrid servers mix Forge mods with Bukkit plugins, which breaks many mods, and most mod authors don't support them.
fix: Run the mods on a plain Forge or NeoForge server, and test there before blaming a mod.

name: Minecraft Comes Alive loads client code on a server
aliases: MCA crash, Minecraft Comes Alive server crash
cause: This version of Minecraft Comes Alive loads client-only game code on a dedicated server when an entity joins the world.
fix: Update Minecraft Comes Alive; if it still crashes, report it to the mod's author.

name: Enigmatic Legacy loads client code on a server
aliases: Enigmatic Legacy crash, EnigmaticEventHandler
cause: Enigmatic Legacy loads client-only code on the server when an entity is attacked, which crashes it as a ticking entity.
fix: Remove Enigmatic Legacy from the server, or ask its author for a server-compatible build.

name: BetterEnd End Stone Smelter crash
aliases: BetterEnd smelter crash, EndStoneSmelterBlockEntity NPE
cause: A BetterEnd bug makes the End Stone Smelter crash when it burns its last fuel item that leaves nothing behind.
fix: Update BetterEnd to 26.101.1 or newer (26.201.0 or newer on Minecraft 26.2).

name: FTB Evolution 2 planter crash
aliases: Agritech planter crash, PlanterExportMixin, Index 14 out of bounds
cause: A mixin in the FTB Evolution 2 companion mod makes an Agritech planter read a slot that doesn't exist.
fix: Update the FTB Evolution 2 modpack to 1.2.0 or newer.

name: Create Spout and cauldron crash
aliases: Create spout crash, Cannot get property level, cauldron crash
signature: Cannot get property IntegerProperty{name=level, clazz=class java.lang.Integer, values=[1, 2, 3]} as it does not exist in Block{minecraft:cauldron}
cause: A Create bug: a Spout keeps filling a cauldron after it has been emptied and reads a fill level the empty cauldron doesn't have.
fix: Update Create to 6.0.9 or newer.

name: Better Enchanting needs Mod Menu on servers
aliases: ModMenuApi ClassNotFoundException, Better Enchanting server crash
cause: Better Enchanting 1.0.1 calls Mod Menu, a client-only mod, from its main code, so dedicated servers crash at start-up.
fix: Update Better Enchanting to a version with the author's fix (pull request #39), or keep it on clients only.

name: Neruina mixin fails to apply
aliases: Neruina crash, Critical injection failure, catchTickingItemStack
cause: Neruina's mixin can't apply to this server's mod set, so the server can't start.
fix: Remove Neruina, or update it to a version that matches the server's Minecraft and Forge.

name: Newest Supplementaries crashes an Arclight server
aliases: Supplementaries server crash, Screen invalid dist
signature: Attempted to load class net/minecraft/client/gui/screens/Screen for invalid dist DEDICATED_SERVER
cause: The poster found that the newest Supplementaries version loaded client-only screen code on their Arclight server.
fix: Use an earlier Supplementaries version on that server, and test on plain Forge.

name: Rubidium or Oculus on a server
aliases: KeyMapping crash, client-only rendering mods on server
signature: Attempted to load class net/minecraft/client/KeyMapping for invalid dist DEDICATED_SERVER
cause: Client-only rendering mods such as Rubidium and Oculus were put on the server.
fix: Remove Rubidium, Oculus and other client-only mods from the server's mods folder.
